# cato_dhcp_settings (Resource)

Manages existing account DHCP settings via networkConfig.dhcp. Destroy removes Terraform ownership and retains remote settings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cato_dhcp_settings" "example" {
  # lease_time = 3600
  # relay = {
  #   enabled = true
  #   timeout = 10
  #   group = { id = cato_dhcp_relay_group.example.id }
  #   # Alternatively: group = { name = "Example relay group" }
  # }
}
# Omission preserves current lease/relay configuration.
# Enabled relay needs an effective timeout and group; disable relay to stop using it.
# Destroy removes Terraform ownership and retains account DHCP settings.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `lease_time` (Number) DHCP lease duration in seconds, minimum 60. Omission preserves its current value.
- `relay` (Attributes) DHCP relay configuration. Omission preserves the current configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--relay))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier. Collection item IDs are opaque and must be preserved unchanged.

<a id="nestedatt--relay"></a>
### Nested Schema for `relay`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable DHCP relay. Enabling requires an effective group and timeout.
- `group` (Attributes) Existing relay group by ID or name. Omission preserves selection; disable relay to stop using it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--relay--group))
- `timeout` (Number) Relay timeout in seconds, 0–90. Omission preserves the value; API cannot clear it.

<a id="nestedatt--relay--group"></a>
### Nested Schema for `relay.group`

Optional:

- `id` (String) Relay group ID
- `name` (String) Relay group name

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cato_dhcp_settings.example ACCOUNT_ID
```
